items.stem: Define the term 'hierarchy'.
items.answer: The levels of management and authority in an organisation, from the most senior to the most junior.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, the levels of management and authority in an organisation, from the most senior to the most junior. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain the link between the span of control and the number of levels of hierarchy.
items.answer: For a given number of employees, wider spans of control mean fewer levels are needed, so the structure is flatter; narrow spans create more levels (a tall structure).
items.markingKey: 1 mark inverse relationship; 1 mark tall v flat. [2]

items.stem: Explain two possible drawbacks of delayering.
items.answer: Remaining managers may be overloaded with wider spans; loss of experienced staff and promotion opportunities can reduce morale; redundancy costs.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark drawback, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Savanna Fresh Ltd is a private limited company based in Nairobi, Kenya. It grows cut flowers and green beans and exports them by air to supermarkets in Europe and employs about 850 people. Its largest European customer has just demanded lower prices and proof of sustainable water use. Explain how delayering could affect the efficiency of Savanna Fresh.
items.answer: Points to develop for Savanna Fresh: delayering removes management levels; lower overhead costs from fewer managers; shorter chain of command speeds decisions; wider spans may reduce control and overload managers.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: delayering removes management levels. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Savanna Fresh: horticulture, about 850 employees, private limited company in Kenya; its largest European customer has just demanded lower prices and proof of sustainable water use). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Savanna Fresh, e.g. lower overhead costs from fewer managers; shorter chain of command speeds decisions; wider spans may reduce control and overload managers. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: IslaConnect Inc. is a private limited company based in Manila, the Philippines. It runs customer-service call centres for banks and airlines in the USA and Australia and employs about 2,600 people. Clients are starting to replace human call handlers with artificial intelligence. Explain the factors that should determine the most suitable span of control for managers at IslaConnect.
items.answer: Points to develop for IslaConnect: span of control = number of direct subordinates; skills and experience of staff; complexity of the tasks; management style and use of technology to monitor work.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: span of control = number of direct subordinates. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (IslaConnect: business process outsourcing, about 2,600 employees, private limited company in the Philippines; clients are starting to replace human call handlers with artificial intelligence). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for IslaConnect, e.g. skills and experience of staff; complexity of the tasks; management style and use of technology to monitor work. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Clients are starting to replace human call handlers with artificial intelligence. IslaConnect Inc., a private limited company in the Philippines with about 2,600 employees, runs customer-service call centres for banks and airlines in the USA and Australia. Evaluate whether IslaConnect should delayer its organisational structure.
items.answer: For: lower costs; faster decisions and communication; empowerment and motivation. Against: overloaded managers; loss of experience and promotion paths; short-term disruption and redundancy costs. Judgement: the decision for IslaConnect depends mainly on the skills of its staff, and also on how fast its market changes.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (IslaConnect: business process outsourcing, about 2,600 employees, private limited company in the Philippines; clients are starting to replace human call handlers with artificial intelligence). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. lower costs; faster decisions and communication; empowerment and motivation; arguments against, e.g. overloaded managers; loss of experience and promotion paths; short-term disruption and redundancy costs. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the skills of its staff; how fast its market changes; how the change is managed. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to IslaConnect, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Clients are starting to replace human call handlers with artificial intelligence. items.answer: Overloaded managers with wide spans.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. overloaded managers with wide spans; fewer promotion opportunities; redundancy costs and low morale among survivors. 1 mark: explained in the context of IslaConnect (business process outsourcing). [2]

items.stem: In an organisation, every manager has a span of control of 3. How many employees are at level 3 of the hierarchy (the managing director is level 1)?
items.markingKey: Level 1: 1; level 2: 3; level 3: 3 × 3 = 9.

items.stem: BatikPay Sdn Bhd has a structure with 5 levels in one division. Everyone above the bottom level has a span of control of 5. Calculate the number of employees at the bottom level and in total.
items.answer: 625 at the bottom level, 781 in total

items.stem: Based in Accra, Gold Coast Cocoa Ltd (private limited company) buys cocoa from local co-operatives and makes premium chocolate bars. The business has around 450 employees. World cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months. (a) Define 'hierarchy'. (b) Explain one advantage to Gold Coast Cocoa of delayering its management structure.
items.answer: (a) The levels of management and authority in an organisation, from the most senior to the most junior. (b) Lower salary costs of managers.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) 1 mark point (lower salary costs of managers; faster communication and decisions; more empowerment for remaining staff), 1 mark explanation, 1 mark application to Gold Coast Cocoa [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'functional structure'.
items.answer: An organisational structure in which the business is divided into departments by function, such as marketing, finance, operations and HR.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, an organisational structure in which the business is divided into departments by function, such as marketing, finance, operations and HR. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of a matrix structure.
items.answer: Advantage: brings together specialists from different functions, improving coordination and innovation on projects. Disadvantage: two bosses can cause conflicting instructions and confusion.
items.markingKey: 1 mark advantage + explanation; 1 mark disadvantage + explanation. [2]

items.stem: Explain why a growing multinational might change from a functional to a divisional structure.
items.answer: As product ranges or markets multiply, divisions allow decisions to be made close to each market and managers to be accountable for each division's profit.
items.markingKey: 1 mark reason; 1 mark explanation. [2]

items.stem: Rising costs of imported packaging have cut its profit margins. Lagos Bites Ltd, a private limited company in Nigeria with about 700 employees, produces packaged snacks such as plantain chips and chin chin. Explain the benefits to Lagos Bites of introducing a matrix structure.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lagos Bites: matrix structure combines functional and project teams; specialists work together on new products such as healthy breakfast cereals; faster and more innovative problem solving; better use of skills across the business.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: matrix structure combines functional and project teams. items.stem: Explain why a functional structure may lead to poor coordination between departments.
items.answer: Departments focus on their own objectives ("silo" thinking), so marketing, operations and finance may not share information or agree priorities.
items.markingKey: 1 mark departmental focus; 1 mark consequence. [2]

items.stem: Define the term 'delegation'.
items.answer: Passing authority to make decisions and complete tasks down the hierarchy to subordinates, while the manager keeps overall responsibility.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, passing authority to make decisions and complete tasks down the hierarchy to subordinates, while the manager keeps overall responsibility. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why delegation might motivate employees.
items.answer: It gives more responsibility, trust and opportunity for achievement, which are Herzberg motivators and help meet esteem and self-actualisation needs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark responsibility/trust; 1 mark motivation theory link. [2]

items.stem: Explain two reasons why a manager may be unwilling to delegate.
items.answer: They may lack trust in subordinates' ability; fear losing control or being blamed for mistakes; think it is quicker to do it themselves.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark reason, 1 mark explanation). [4]
